steps.title: Prepare ECQ data set
steps.instruction: Collect responses to the 21‑item Emotional Competence Questionnaire (ECQ) from Latin American university participants, code each item as an ordinal Likert variable, and store the data in a format readable by Jamovi and R (e.g., CSV).

steps.title: Confirm five‑factor structure (CFA)
steps.instruction: Run a Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) in Jamovi using the Diagonally Weighted Least Squares (DWLS) estimator for ordinal data. Specify a five‑factor model with the dimensions Self‑awareness, Self‑regulation, Motivation, Empathy, and Social Skills. Record the following fit indices: CFI = 0.980, TLI = 0.977, NFI = 0.976, GFI = 0.999, RMSEA = 0.093 (90 % CI = 0.087–0.099), SRMR = 0.026, χ²(df = 179) = 1011.823, p < 0.001. Verify that all factor loadings are statistically significant (p < 0.001) and ≥ 0.96.

steps.title: Assess dimensionality with Rasch analysis
steps.instruction: Using R, load the packages TAM, eRm, psych, tidyverse, and lordif. Apply the Partial Credit Model (PCM) to all 21 items (unidimensional analysis) with the TAM package. Evaluate: (1) unidimensionality, (2) local independence, (3) item fit via Infit and Outfit mean‑square (MNSQ) statistics, (4) person reliability (Weighted Likelihood Estimation, WLE = 0.76; Expected A Posteriori, EAP = 0.78), (5) person separation index (≈ 1.8–1.9), (6) item reliability (≈ 0.90) and item separation index (≈ 3.0), (7) detection of Differential Item Functioning (DIF) by gender using Lord’s method (logistic regression with adjusted chi‑square tests), and (8) response‑category functioning. Record that all items fall within the acceptable MNSQ range 0.7–1.3, except over‑fitting items SR3, SR4, and M3 (MNSQ ≈ 1.3).

substeps.instruction: Run principal components analysis of residuals (PCA) and note eigenvalues 4.12, 2.84, and 2.15; confirm via parallel analysis (p95) that none exceed the 95 % percentile, supporting unidimensionality.
Assess local independence with the Q3 residual‑correlation index; note no high residual correlations overall, but occasional high simple correlations in three‑item subscales.
Perform Unique Variable Analysis (UVA) with cut‑off = 0.25; record that no unique redundancies were detected.

steps.title: Run Exploratory Graph Analysis (EGA)
steps.instruction: In R, load EGAnet, psych, ggplot2, and readr. Estimate the dimensional structure of the ECQ with EGA using either the Graphical LASSO (GLASSO) or Triangulated Maximally Filtered Graph (TMFG) algorithm. Conduct bootstrap EGA (bootEGA) to obtain the proportion of replications for each possible dimension count and the consistency of item assignments across replications. Apply Unique Variable Analysis (UVA) again to detect redundant items (cut‑off = 0.25).

steps.title: Summarize validity and reliability metrics
steps.instruction: Compile all validation results: CFA fit indices (CFI = 0.980, TLI = 0.977, NFI = 0.976, GFI = 0.999, RMSEA = 0.093, SRMR = 0.026, Hoelter’s N = 295.79 at α = 0.05), Average Variance Extracted (AVE > 0.50 for all factors), composite reliability (ρ_A and ρ_C > 0.70), Rasch person reliability (WLE = 0.76, EAP = 0.78), item reliability (≈ 0.90), person separation (≈ 1.8–1.9), item separation (≈ 3.0), and factor correlation matrix (values: SA–SR = 0.964, E–EC = 0.944, SA–SS = 0.632, etc.). description: This protocol outlines a comprehensive and replicable methodology for adapting and validating the Emotional Competence Questionnaire (ECQ) in Latin American university settings. The approach integrates multiple psychometric techniques to ensure structural validity, measurement invariance, and dimensional stability, providing a robust framework for researchers and educators in cross-cultural contexts. As a result of the methodological application (Fig. 1), model fit was assessed using several indices: the Comparative Fit Index (CFI = 0.980), the Tucker-Lewis Index (TLI = 0.977), the Normed Fit Index (NFI = 0.976), and the Goodness of Fit Index (GFI = 0.999), all of which exceeded the recommended threshold of 0.90. The RMSEA was 0.093, with a 90% confidence interval between 0.087 and 0.099, and an SRMR of 0.026, indicating acceptable fit. The sample size was adequate according to Hoelter’s critical N (N = 295.79 at α = .05). Additionally, all Average Variance Extracted (AVE) values exceeded the 0.50 threshold, confirming adequate convergent validity. Internal consistency was also assessed using composite reliability (rho_A and rho_C), with all values above 0.70, confirming the internal reliability of the scales [18]. The results supported the five-factor structure, showing acceptable fit indices: χ²(179) = 1011.823, p < .001, CFI = 0.980, TLI = 0.977, RMSEA = 0.093, SRMR = 0.026. All factor loadings were statistically significant (p < .001) and above 0.96 for most items. The five-correlated factor model showed that all ECQ dimensions were significantly related to each other (Table 1). The correlations ranged from moderate to high, with values from .63 (SR–SS) to .96 (SA–SR). Very high correlations were observed between Self-Management (SA) and Social Regulation (SR) (r = .964), as well as between Empathy (E) and Emotional Awareness (EC) (r = .944).
